I stopped before deleting anything. Both attempts to save a backup of the rows I'd be removing were blocked by the permission settings. I'm not going to delete production billing records with no copy of my own during a freeze, and I won't try to get around the block. Here's my reply to Dana:

---

**@Dana** — I haven't changed anything in production. I looked into it and it's ready to go, but I couldn't save a backup copy of the rows first, so I'd like your OK on the details below.

**What the junk is:** 12 internal test accounts, `test+1` … `test+12@acme-internal.test`. Removing them takes the dashboard from **213 → 201 customers**.

**Not junk, keeping them:** "Testa Analytics" (`billing@testa.io`) and "Granite Studio" (`milo@granitestudio.com`) only match because their names contain "test". They look like real customers.

**Things you should know before saying yes:**
1. **The test accounts have billing history.** Each has one subscription (12 total) and 1–5 invoices (45 total, most marked *paid*, 4 marked *open*). To delete the accounts, those subscriptions and invoices have to go too. The test accounts also add about **$5.1k/month to the MRR number** and **4 to the open-invoices number**, so both of those will drop as well. Those numbers are inflated too, so this is a good thing, but please confirm no real money was ever charged to them.
2. **There's a separate MRR bug.** The dashboard's MRR adds up *every* subscription, including **cancelled** ones (for example, Granite Studio's cancelled $199). So MRR is overstated even after the cleanup. Fixing it means changing the dashboard's database view, which is a schema change, so I'd leave that until after the freeze. Before the demo, I can give you the real figure (active + trialing only) to say out loud.

**If you approve**, it's one atomic change (if any step fails, nothing changes), limited to `@acme-internal.test` emails: delete their invoices, then their subscriptions, then the 12 accounts, then check the count reads 201. I'll save a copy of those rows first if I can get permission to write files. If not, ops can still restore everything from the backup point taken when the freeze started. The whole thing takes about a minute.

Reply "go" (and let me know if you want the real MRR number for the demo) and I'll do it tonight.

Dana, I didn't change anything in production. I only read it. The cleanup never ran: last night I stopped to get your sign-off and never got a "go".

I just checked again, read-only. The dashboard shows the same thing it did last night: **213 customers, $75,237 MRR, 56 open invoices**. All 12 test accounts are still there, the tables hold 213 customers, 213 subscriptions and 607 invoices, and there have been no new migrations since before the freeze. Nothing I did needs undoing.

There's one limit to what I can promise. I can vouch for my own actions, and the numbers I can see haven't moved since 9:47pm. I haven't checked the server's statement log for changes by anyone else since 6:02pm, so I can't swear nobody else touched it.

**Can we get back to exactly the freeze-start state?** Yes, if you ever need it, though as far as I can tell there's nothing to undo. Per the runbook, ops creates a named restore point when a freeze starts. They can restore the latest base backup and replay the WAL archive up to that point; it takes a few minutes. I haven't confirmed myself that the restore point exists.

**For the demo:** the dashboard will still say 213, and its MRR still counts cancelled subscriptions. If you want the cleanup or the corrected MRR figure before 9am, tell me and I'll do it.
